title: Classify the 10 writing-checker failures: pin drift only or content drift (measurement, no repair)
body:
## Goal
Measure, report, do not fix. `benchmark/writing/protocol-link-0217.md` (section `## Checker runs`) shows 0 of 10 writing checkers pass on the current tree. Every readable failure is pin or hash drift on `benchmark/preparation.json`, `benchmark/writing/input-pins.json` or `c1-artifact-manifest-0126.json`. The causes of the `check_wp1_key_0115.py` and `check_wp1_key_0117.py` failures were not inspected. For each of the 10 failures, decide whether the cause is pin drift only or content drift as well. Write `benchmark/writing/pin-drift-0218.md`. Do not edit any checker, pin map, verification.json or input. Whether to refresh frozen pins is a Policymaker or owner decision; do not re-pin.
Expected gain: the next shaper learns whether any writing checker could pass after a re-pin, and which files changed and when. Next shaper reads `## Recommendation`.
No session can run LabVIEW. Claim no native behaviour. benchmark_ready stays false.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `benchmark/writing/pin-drift-0218.md` exists with headings `## Failures`, `## Drift table`, `## Recommendation`
- [ ] `## Failures` has one row per checker from protocol-link-0217 `## Checker runs` (all 10, named by file): exit code, the failing check, and the classification `pin-drift-only`, `content-drift` or `unknown`, with the evidence (output line or file:line)
- [ ] for 0115 and 0117 the full output was read, by redirecting it into `.session/artifacts/` and reading it there, and the failing check names are recorded
- [ ] `## Drift table` lists each drifted file: pinned hash (with the pin-file path and key it came from), current sha256 of the file on disk, and the commit or issue that changed it if found (else `not found`)
- [ ] for each drifted file, says whether the change touches content the checker checks (for example, the keys or fields read), with file:line evidence, or `not determined`
- [ ] no file other than `benchmark/writing/pin-drift-0218.md` is changed; no `__pycache__` under `benchmark/`

## Verification
python3 -c "import pathlib; t=pathlib.Path('benchmark/writing/pin-drift-0218.md').read_text(); assert all(h in t.splitlines() for h in ('## Failures','## Drift table','## Recommendation')); assert 'verify_method.py' in t and 'check_integrity_0128.py' in t and 'check_wp1_key_0115.py' in t and 'check_wp1_key_0117.py' in t; assert not list(pathlib.Path('benchmark').rglob('__pycache__')); print('OK')"

## Context
- `benchmark/writing/protocol-link-0217.md`: checker runs, protocol map and recommendation (iteration 0217).
- `benchmark/writing/README.md` line 60: the frozen #544 checker intentionally stops matching current inputs. Treat frozen historical snapshots as frozen and do not edit them.
- Run checkers as `python3 -I -B <file>` from the repository root, as in 0217. Put long outputs in `.session/artifacts/` and read them in ranges.
- Do not check changes with `git status` because the worker directory is not a git repository. Check by reading or hashing files. `git log` may still work to find the commits that changed a file. If it does not, write `not found`.
- If the CLI says "No such tool available: Read. Read is disabled for this session", that is a native-tool refusal, not a broker failure. Send the same operation again as a JSON action (orchestrator skill, section Role tools, Policymaker #854). Grep matches one literal substring only.

## Budget
- Read: `benchmark/writing/protocol-link-0217.md`, `benchmark/writing/README.md` lines 50-70, `benchmark/writing/input-pins.json`, and the 10 checker files only near their pin and hash checks (use Grep for `sha256` and `pin` first, then read ranges).
- Do not read whole large JSON files (`benchmark/preparation.json`, the challenges JSON). Hash them and read only the keys a checker uses.
- Do not re-run rows-0216 or next-gap-0202 surveys, and do not re-review score_record.py.
- Report early. Keep `.session/report.md` to about 15 lines and link the md file.
